item.title: Warming could help make the Indian Ocean a stronger climate buffer
item.description: The world's oceans help slow climate change by absorbing carbon dioxide (CO₂) from the atmosphere, but how much they take up can vary throughout the year. New research, published in Geophysical Research Letters, suggests these seasonal patterns are changing across the Indian Ocean, potentially affecting how it helps to regulate Earth's climate. Fuente: Phys.org.

A hurricane warning remained in effect from Manzanillo in Colima state to Cabo Corrientes in Jalisco. The latest NHC data showed the Category 2 hurricane with maximum sustained winds of 105 mph (165kph) moving northwest off Mexico’s Pacific coast at 10 mph (17kph). item.title: Florida opens $191.8M water plant to protect the Matanzas River and conserve drinking water
item.description: St. Johns County Utilities officials celebrated the completion of the State Road 207 Water Reclamation Facility. This facility, costing $191.8 million, will treat wastewater and provide reclaimed water for irrigation purposes. The project aims to reduce dependence on the Floridan Aquifer, especially during ongoing drought conditions. Capacity of the facility can be expanded to meet future demand while preventing nutrient pollution in local waters. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.description: Iboga root, central to several Gabonese ritual traditions, is believed to have huge potential for use in treating addiction and some mental illnesses The temple is dark, its sandy floor edged with candles. People sit shoulder to shoulder beneath palm fronds hung from the rafters. Through the night, they swallow what they have come here for: a bitter root bark called iboga. Tabernanthe iboga is a slow-growing central African rainforest shrub, the root bark of which has long been used in several Gabonese ritual traditions. Continue reading... item.title: EPA quietly backtracks on claims US has phased out toxic Pfas compounds
item.description: Agency changes wording on website as Texas-based chemical firm continues manufacture of plastic containers The Environmental Protection Agency has quietly backtracked on a claim that the US has phased out two of the most dangerous Pfas compounds – Pfoa and Pfos. The EPA has found that virtually no level of exposure to either in drinking water is safe, and the International Agency for Research on Cancer classifies Pfoa as “carcinogenic to humans” and Pfos as “possibly carcinogenic”. Still, the EPA is allowing Houston-based Inhance to produce containers from which Pfoa has been found to leach… Fuente: The Guardian - Environment.

item.title: US workers facing deadly heat borrow from tomato pickers to win key protections
item.description: As efforts to protect people from extreme heat stall, organizers are embracing an approach that targets major brands’ reputations “It’s the kind of heat that makes you feel like you’re being dehydrated, like your skin is drying out,” said Lucas Benitez, after harvesting watermelons with his sons and wife this summer. “The heat that we had 30 years ago is not nearly the heat that we have today.” This summer was the hottest on record in the US, and most workers in fields, greenhouses and unconditioned indoor facilities still do not have heat protections on the job, putting their health at risk… Fuente: The Guardian - Environment.

item.title: The ambiguous costs of climate change
item.description: As human activity has increased temperatures globally, determining the costs directly incurred by climate change is challenging. item.title: Supercooled clouds over the highest mountains respond differently to climate change
item.description: Most studies of how clouds are responding to climate change focus on clouds over the oceans, rather than over mountains. Those that do focus on mountain clouds tend to explore cloud microphysics rather than long-term trends in cloud phase. But understanding cloud behavior over regions such as the Tibetan Plateau, which supplies water to hundreds of millions of people, is critical—especially as diminishing snowpack and altered precipitation patterns threaten this critical water source. Fuente: Phys.org.

The combination of heat and dryness has amplified fire risks, with strong winds anticipated. Firefighters are actively battling flames in areas like Malibu and Azusa, urging locals to stay alert. In an effort to mitigate fire hazards, precautionary power outages have been instituted across numerous regions. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Japan Mistakenly Issues Warning for Strongest Ever Earthquake
item.description: Officials on Friday withdrew an alert sent when they believed a 9.9-magnitude earthquake had taken place. In the end, the tremor was hardly felt. Fuente: The New York Times - World.

item.title: Duct tape kept out more floodwater than sandbags in laboratory tests
item.description: Could a cheap roll of duct tape help protect your home from flooding? New research suggests it could make a surprisingly big difference. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: How do combined sewer overflows affect water quality in Philadelphia?
item.description: In Philadelphia and many urban areas across the U.S. with sewer systems dating back to the 1800s, more frequent flooding is posing a threat not only to people and property but also to surrounding ecosystems. In these areas, stormwater and sewage drain into the same pipes, which are designed to spill into nearby waterways when flooding occurs rather than inundating streets. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Francia: del vino al pistacho, la nueva apuesta de los viticultores ante el cambio climático
item.description: En Francia, los viticultores intentan adaptarse a los desafíos a los que se enfrentan: el calentamiento global y la caída del consumo de vino. Para hacer frente a estos problemas, han decidido diversificar sus cultivos. Fuente: France 24 - Español.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Ártico y Antártida pierden hielo: ¿qué significa para el nivel del mar?
item.description: Los polos siguen mostrando señales del cambio climático. En 2026, la extensión del hielo marino del Ártico alcanzó uno de sus diez mínimos más bajos desde que comenzaron las mediciones por satélite. Por su parte, un análisis internacional de IMBIE calcula que la pérdida de hielo de Groenlandia y la Antártida elevó el nivel medio global del mar en unos 3,1 centímetros entre 1979 y 2023. ¿Qué revelan estos datos sobre la evolución del deshielo y sus consecuencias para las zonas costeras? Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: For restaurants Covid-19 was a crisis – pandemic loans are proving a disaster
item.description: Low-interest loans kept many eateries afloat. But the industry never recovered enough for them to repay the debt For almost 20 years, Jai Mazumdar has served vegetarian curries, samosas, gulab jamun and other Indian delicacies at Spice N Curry, a cafe and grocery nestled inside a modest strip mall near Florida International University (FIU) in Miami. When the Covid-19 pandemic devastated his business, as it did with so many restaurants, Mazumdar took out a $370,000 economic injury disaster loan (EIDL) from the federal government in early 2021. At the time, it provided a desperately needed… Fuente: The Guardian - Environment.

item.title: Guterres urges faster action and financing to stop biodiversity loss
item.description: The United Nations Secretary-General appealed on Friday for governments, businesses and communities to accelerate efforts to protect biodiversity for future generations and all life on Earth. Fuente: UN News.

item.title: Biodiversidad, Día de la Alimentación, niños de Gaza, empresas tecnológicas… Las noticias del viernes
item.description: El mundo se comprometió a proteger solo el 30% de la tierra y los mares, y no va camino de lograrlo. El Niño amenaza con agravar el hambre en América Latina. 340 niños han muerto en Gaza en el último año a pesar del alto el fuego. Un experto pide controlar a las empresas tecnológicas para evitar abusos en países que salen de conflictos. Fuente: Noticias ONU.

item.title: Ante el aumento de los desastres climáticos, la próxima cumbre del clima COP31 afronta una prueba de confianza
item.description: A menos de un mes de la próxima conferencia de la ONU sobre el cambio climático COP31 en Antalya, Türkiye, representantes de las presidencias de tres cumbres consecutivas se reunieron en Nueva York ante una pregunta apremiante: ¿cómo recuperar la confianza en la acción climática internacional cuando las consecuencias del calentamiento global ya se sienten en todo el planeta? Fuente: Noticias ONU.

item.title: La naturaleza, en peligro: Guterres reclama un impulso mundial para protegerla
item.description: El mundo está lejos de cumplir su promesa de proteger el 30% de las tierras y los mares del planeta para 2030. A pocos días de la COP17 sobre biodiversidad, el titular de la ONU pide a Gobiernos y empresas que aceleren las medidas para frenar la destrucción de la naturaleza y reorienten hacia su conservación miles de millones de dólares que hoy financian actividades perjudiciales para el medioambiente. Fuente: Noticias ONU.

item.title: Singapore targets 7 companies over wildfires in Indonesia as toxic haze worsens
item.description: Singapore has identified seven companies it says were involved in wildfires in Indonesia that are choking the city state with haze, and plans to issue notices requiring them to take preventive measures, the Business Times reported. The companies will receive notices under the Transboundary Haze Pollution Act requiring them to stop or refrain from burning and submit plans to prevent a recurrence, the newspaper reported, citing Sustainability and the Environment Minister Grace Fu at a Friday press... item.title: Hurricane Trudy becomes major Category 3 storm near Mexico's Pacific Coast
item.description: The emergence of Hurricane Trudy has escalated into a powerful Category 3 storm, targeting Mexico's Pacific coastline with maximum sustained winds reaching 120 mph. A hurricane warning is now in effect from Cabo Corrientes to Punta San Telmo. As this significant weather event unfolds, Tropical Storm Simon is anticipated to dwindle, while another system, Champi, progresses near Guam, prompting authorities to issue various warnings. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Japan issued a 9.9 magnitude earthquake alert, but ground didn't shake: What happened
item.description: An "alert" indicating a massive magnitude-9.9 earthquake sent shockwaves of fear across Japan on Friday afternoon. Just eight minutes after its issuance, the Japan Meteorological Agency retracted the warning, which had been triggered by a lesser magnitude-6.9 quake off the Kamchatka Peninsula in Russia. Although the alert caused temporary disruptions in transportation, officials are now investigating the warning system to ensure public safety and prevent future confusion. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Flash floods destroy villages in central Nepal
item.description: Landslide blocks river and triggers downstream flooding, while summer temperatures persist in Portugal Flash floods have swept through Nepal’s central Gorkha district after a pre-dawn landslide on 11 October blocked the Budhi Gandaki River, triggering severe downstream flooding. Two villages in the worst-affected Chumanubri rural municipality were reportedly destroyed, with homes, roads and bridges washed away. Part of a hydropower station was also damaged. After river levels surged from 2 metres to nearly 8.5 metres within hours, the national disaster risk reduction and management authority… Publicado también por: The Guardian - Environment. item.title: Iguazu Falls in South America hits record 10 times normal water flow – video
item.description: Iguazu Falls, an Unesco world heritage site, has reached a record water flow after heavy rains across the river basin. El Niño weather patterns are said to have driven the water flow to hit 10 times the normal amount. Usually the water flow is 1.5m litres per second, but local government registered a flow of 15m litres of water per second. Argentina temporarily closes Iguazu Falls after El Niño-fuelled surge in water levels Continue reading... Fuente: The Guardian - Environment.

item.title: Queensland protects 396,000 hectares of cattle stations, safeguarding wetlands and threatened birds
item.description: Queensland proudly announces the acquisition of three significant cattle properties, expanding its protected area network by almost 396,000 hectares. These lands are essential for wildlife conservation, providing critical habitats for various threatened species. Funded by the federal government through a biodiversity initiative, this move contributes to Australia's ambitious target of safeguarding 30 percent of its land and oceans by 2030. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: EU backs trade ‘kill switch’, China exports surge, third-quarter GDP
item.description: European Union leaders supported creating a tool to potentially shut out Chinese goods as a growing flood of low-cost imports pushed the bilateral trade deficit to a record. Officials could start work on developing a trade “kill switch”, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen signalled to EU leaders at a Brussels meeting on Thursday, the South China Morning Post reported, citing unidentified people briefed on the talks. Leaders requested a proposal by year-end, Bloomberg News said.... Fuente: South China Morning Post.
